subject_line: From home inspection reports to Ink Earl
email_body:
Dear Susan,

I've been reading about your poetry, from Joy Is So Exhausting, with its poems built from home inspection reports and Lorca, through the Governor General's shortlisting of Throaty Wipes, to Ink Earl, shortlisted for the 2022 ReLit Award. I'd love to ask how borrowed forms and source texts still shape what you write, and what changed in your approach between Throaty Wipes and Ink Earl.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Ink Earl (2021) shortlisted for 2022 ReLit; Throaty Wipes GG-shortlisted 2016; Joy Is So Exhausting uses home inspection reports and Lorca as source texts (Wikipedia/Coach House blurb). Email seen in search result on UWindsor English faculty profile.

subject_line: Touch the Darkness and Windsor's first Poet Laureate
email_body:
Dear Marty,

Touch the Darkness caught my attention because it gathers the poems you wrote after becoming Windsor's first Poet Laureate in 2011, alongside decades of running Black Moss Press. I'd be interested to hear how an official civic role changed what you noticed in the city, and whether writing as Poet Laureate felt different from the poems you had published before it.

subject_line: La voix, de M'accompagne à La langue de ta langue
email_body:
Bonjour Marc André,

J'ai été frappé par la continuité entre votre poésie, de Carnets de Brigance (prix Desjardins) et M'accompagne (prix Louis-Guillaume) jusqu'à La langue de ta langue en 2021, et votre travail sur la poésie en scène, la voix et la corporéité. J'aimerais vous demander comment ce travail sur la poésie dite à voix haute a influencé l'écriture de La langue de ta langue.

The Author Ledger est un projet indépendant consacré à de courts portraits d'auteurs. Chaque portrait se construit à partir de quelques questions écrites, auxquelles vous répondez à votre rythme, et le texte complet vous est soumis pour relecture avant publication.

Seriez-vous ouvert à y participer ? Sans aucune pression.

Bien cordialement,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: La langue de ta langue (2021); prix Desjardins for Carnets de Brigance, prix Louis-Guillaume for M'accompagne; co-directs Poésie en scène research on voice and corporeality (Percées UQAM). Email seen in search result on UQAM professor profile (per earlier agents).

subject_line: Jackie Kennedy at the Lady Chatterley hearing in Tenderness
email_body:
Dear Alison,

What stays with me about Tenderness is the way it braids D. H. Lawrence's writing of Lady Chatterley's Lover with the 1960 obscenity trial, and then adds Jackie Kennedy attending the American hearing before she became First Lady. I understand you stepped back from your Chichester professorship to research it full-time. I'd love to ask how you decided which historical threads to follow and where invention was allowed to enter.

subject_line: Elinor and the True Cause in Forbidden
email_body:
Dear Judy,

I was drawn to Forbidden, where fifteen-year-old Elinor has grown up inside the True Cause, and a chance meeting with Jaime in the woods begins to unsettle everything she has been told. Kirkus noted how closely you stay inside her perspective. Having published over forty books, from picture books to YA, I'd love to ask how you found Elinor's voice, and how your Wordtamer work on creativity feeds back into your fiction.
